initiatives.name: Net Zero Transition Programme
initiatives.summary: Standard Life is committed to being a net zero business by 2050, having exceeded its 25% 2025 interim portfolio decarbonisation target (achieving 58% reduction) and is on track for a 2030 50% reduction target. The company also plans to invest up to £40 billion in sustainable, transition and UK-focused productive assets.

evidence.title: Net Zero Transition Plan with 2030 and 2050 targets
evidence.summary: Standard Life is committed to being a net zero business by 2050, having exceeded its 25% 2025 interim portfolio decarbonisation target (achieving 58% reduction) and is on track for a 2030 50% reduction target. The company also plans to invest up to £40 billion in sustainable, transition and UK-focused productive assets.
evidence.quote: We have exceeded our 25% 2025 interim portfolio decarbonisation target and under most scenarios are on track for our 2030 50% reduction target. Our long-term ambition is to invest up to £40 billion in sustainable, transition and UK-focused productive assets.

evidence.title: Operational emissions reduction target revised to 90% by 2030
evidence.summary: The Group achieved an 84% reduction in emissions intensity (Scope 1 and 2 per FTE) against its 2019 baseline, surpassing its prior 75-85% target. It has now set a new, more ambitious target of a 90% reduction in absolute Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2030 or sooner.
evidence.quote: We previously set a target to reach net zero operational emissions by 2025 including by offsetting our residual emissions, this was based on emerging best practice. In line with current best practice, we are now targeting a 90% reduction in our Scope 1 and 2 absolute emissions, which we aim to achieve by 2030 or sooner.

evidence.title: Updated Net Zero Transition Plan for publication March 2026
evidence.summary: The Sustainability Committee challenged proposals for the Group's updated Net Zero Transition Plan, scheduled for publication in March 2026, as part of ongoing sustainability strategy oversight.
evidence.quote: Challenged the proposals for the Group’s updated Net Zero Transition Plan, for publication in March 2026.

initiatives.name: Cost Savings and Deleveraging Programme
initiatives.summary: The Group is executing a cost savings programme targeting £250 million of annual run-rate cost savings by end-2026, net of inflation, relative to 2023 cost levels, largely through technology-driven simplification of its operating model. £180 million has been delivered cumulatively across 2024-25, ahead of schedule.
initiatives.investmentSummary: £250 million annual run-rate target; £180 million delivered 2024-25

evidence.title: £250 million annual run-rate cost savings programme
evidence.summary: The Group is executing a cost savings programme targeting £250 million of annual run-rate cost savings by end-2026, net of inflation, relative to 2023 cost levels, largely through technology-driven simplification of its operating model. £180 million has been delivered cumulatively across 2024-25, ahead of schedule.
evidence.quote: The Group’s cost savings programme remains firmly on track to deliver the end-2026 targeted £250 million of annual run-rate cost savings, net of inflation, relative to the Group’s 2023 cost levels, as we continue to enhance our business and progress towards a more efficient Group-wide operating model. In 2025, £117 million of run-rate savings were delivered, which combined with the savings achieved in 2024, brings the cumulative run-rate cost savings total to £180 million across 2024–25, £55 million ahead of our original delivery profile by 2025.

evidence.title: Balance sheet deleveraging to c.30% Solvency II leverage
evidence.summary: The Group is executing a deleveraging programme targeting a c.30% Solvency II leverage ratio by end of 2026, using surplus cash to repay historic M&A-related debt. In 2025, debt repayments of c.£200 million (February) and c.£200 million (December) improved the leverage ratio to 33%.
evidence.quote: In February 2025 we repaid c.£200 million of debt, with a further c.£200 million redeemed in December 2025. Our Solvency II leverage ratio at the end of December improved to 33% (2024: 36%) and we are on track for a ratio of c.30% by the end of 2026.
